learningObjective: Reason about the O(S^2) HBM footprint of naive attention and its scaling implication for long sequences.

canonicalClaims.claim: Naive three-kernel scaled-dot-product attention writes and reads the [S,S] intermediate `S = QK^T` and softmax result `P` to/from HBM per (batch, head); memory cost scales as O(S^2), which becomes the dominant bottleneck for long sequences.
conditions: Standard three-kernel decomposition without tiled online softmax.
nonImplications: Does not imply naive attention is slower than FlashAttention at small S.
Does not imply intermediates can be kept in FP16 without precision issues.

misconceptions.claim: Naive attention is compute-bound at all sequence lengths.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For long sequences, S^2 memory traffic dominates.

misconceptions.claim: FP16 intermediates are automatically kept in registers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Register file cannot hold S x S tensors; they spill to HBM without tiled algorithms.

misconceptions.claim: The S x S intermediate is virtual and never materialized.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In three-kernel naive attention, it is materialized between kernels.

misconceptions.claim: The problem can be solved simply by using FP16 intermediates.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Halves storage but does not change the quadratic scaling nor address numerical instability.

implementationFacts: FlashAttention avoids materialization via tiled online softmax + fused Q/K/V/O access.
For S=8192, one (B=1, H=1) head is 128 MB for S alone in FP16.
